entities.summary: The County of Flanders was one of the most powerful political entities in the medieval Low Countries, located on the North Sea coast of modern-day Belgium and north-eastern France. Unlike the neighbouring states of Brabant and Hainaut, it was within the territory of the Kingdom of France. The counts of Flanders held the most northerly part of the kingdom, and were among the original twelve peers of France. For centuries, the economic activity of the Flemish cities, such as Ghent, Bruges,Ypres and Lille, made Flanders one of the most affluent regions in Europe, and also gave them strong international connections to trading partners.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The County of Flanders played a crucial role in shaping European trade and commerce during the medieval period, with its cities such as Ghent and Bruges serving as major hubs for textile production and international trade. The region's economic prosperity had significant regional impact, contributing to the cultural and artistic developments of the time.
